task: This is a synthetic writing exercise. Using these fictional reporting notes, write a newspaper news story for general readers. Draw only on the supplied notes; do not invent additional reported events, scenes, or quotations. Write from this reporting snapshot as of August 22, 2024. Include a headline. Target 450 to 650 words. Follow AP style.

facts.text: TeleLink Rural Networks announced on August 22, 2024, that it had completed fiber-optic broadband connections to 78,000 previously unserved households in Clearwater County, eight months ahead of the contract schedule.
The project was funded through a $440 million federal broadband equity grant and $450 million in state infrastructure bonds, for a total project cost of $890 million.
The rollout used aerial cable installation along existing utility poles for 84% of the connections, reducing permitting time and underground excavation costs.

TeleLink CEO Rachel Auer said: "We finished early because we standardized the aerial installation process and trained crews to achieve 150 connections per day per team rather than the industry standard of 90."
The delivered service provides symmetrical speeds of 1 gigabit per second at a monthly retail price of $65.
Prior to the project, 74% of the county's rural households had access only to satellite or fixed wireless internet with speeds below 25 megabits per second.
The county school district said 4,200 students gained access to home broadband through the project, eliminating a documented gap in homework completion rates between rural and town students.

Clearwater County Board chair James Moran said two agricultural businesses had relocated operations from neighboring counties in anticipation of the fiber project; he credited the connection as enabling precision agriculture monitoring.
The project required installation of 2,300 kilometers of new fiber cable and 140 distribution nodes.
Take-up rates exceeded projections: 61% of connected households subscribed within the first 90 days, compared to the contract's 50% 18-month target.
The $890 million project serves the 78,000 households at an average cost of approximately $11,400 per household.
TeleLink built the infrastructure under a 25-year indefeasible right-of-use agreement with the county; ownership of the fiber network transfers to the county at the agreement's end.
Federal broadband rules required TeleLink to offer a $30-per-month low-income tier; as of August, 9,200 households had enrolled in the low-income plan.
Two neighboring counties with similar broadband gaps are expected to begin their own federal grant-funded projects in 2025.
Auer said early completion will allow TeleLink to redeploy its installation teams to a second project in another state, improving the company's capital efficiency.
The federal grant included a clawback provision requiring repayment if fewer than 40% of connected households subscribe within five years.
Workforce development officials noted that 140 of the 380 installation crew members hired for the project were from Clearwater County, with training provided through a TeleLink partnership program.
The county's broadband gap had been documented since 2015; two previous project proposals failed due to insufficient funding.
Healthcare officials said telehealth visit rates among county residents with newly connected households increased threefold in the first six months of availability.
The broadband equity grant program was authorized by Congress in 2021; Clearwater County's project is among the first 40 completions nationally under the program.
